correctness.rationale: Proof of exact state-graph/root bijection, BFS shortest-distance and shortest-path count invariant; full integer source enumerations through k=8. Rooted counts 1,2,2,8,40,6272,768; independent Held-Karp compulsory-palindrome overlap DP reproduces optimum length and matching tour counts and tests constructive witnesses. Computations performed from the actual source files, not logs alone. No unbounded extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Knowing a minimum linear length and counts of the linear strings does not determine how many cyclic covering strings have a marked all-zero window: additional wraparound-only covered strings may occur. The cyclic rooted multiplicities are not corollaries of those databases. The infinite all-palindromes generation results in 2010 do not subsume finite optimal-cycle counts.

Orenstein et al. (2013), Results, require one k-mer from every reverse-complement pair in a DNA alphabet. Ordinary reversal-palindrome mandatory edges are a different pattern set.
Anisiu et al. (2010), §2–4, give structural and enumeration claims for palindrome factors, not the cyclic optimal-count table.

originality.rationale: Exact linear length and multiplicity databases were found and explicitly excluded from novelty. The statement concerns distinct rooted shortest cyclic word counts; OEIS A390882 gives linear counts 960 and 176 at orders 7,8 versus rooted cyclic 6272 and 768. Full-text primary sources cover different objects or weaker existence/noncompactness results. Residual unindexed cyclic count literature risk remains.
residual_risks: Search and available primary sources cannot prove universal novelty; an unindexed exhaustive count of rooted cyclic optimal palindrome covers could coincide.
The shortest lengths are already tabulated for linear superstrings and are not claimed original.
The main theorem is finite up to order 8, not a claimed asymptotic or infinite classification.

value.rationale: The multiplicity of minimum-length periodic libraries covering all fixed-length binary palindromes is a natural design-enumeration invariant, not inferred from minimum linear lengths or their counts. The drop 6272 to 768 with sixteen mandatory patterns at both orders is a meaningful sharp finite structural contrast; orders 2–8 form the first complete regime with <=16 mandatory patterns; n=9 jumps to 32.
